title: Asymmetric cryptography: RSA, elliptic curves and key size

videos.script: Lesson 1 left a problem open. Two machines that have never met cannot share a secret key. {{title}} Asymmetric cryptography answers it with a pair of keys. One is public and can be handed to anybody. The other is private and never leaves its owner. {{pair}} The two are tied together by mathematics, and the tie only runs one way. From the private key you can compute the public one. From the public key, nobody can work back. {{derive}} RSA builds that one-way tie from multiplying two large primes. {{rsa}} Elliptic curves build it from a different problem, and they need far smaller keys. {{curves}} Then the question every configuration file asks. How many bits is enough? {{sizes}} By the end of this lesson you can read a key file and say what it is, and whether it is strong enough.
